summary: Midflight proxy upgrade causes websocket handoff to drop terminal JSON object and leave truncated choice
description:
Issue summary: During a high-throughput window on 2026-03-10, AtlasApps reported that long-running WebSocket streams occasionally end with a partial JSON 'choice' object and no terminal metadata (end_event). Client logs show the final JSON object missing closing braces and the 'metadata' field absent. Impact: Several production chat flows returned truncated final sentences, sometimes causing downstream parsers to throw and the customer to re-request completions, doubling token usage and affecting SLAs.

Environment: Production (eu-west), requests routed through our edge proxy pool behind a CDN with active health checks and transparent connection rebinds. A small subset of requests go through an older proxy flavor that performs an in-flight socket upgrade to another edge on backend health probe.

Observed behavior: Client receives partial JSON chunk (last text tokens present, no "end" event). WS connection is closed by the client after a short timeout; server logs show an abrupt EOF on the upstream socket around the same timestamp. No end-event was recorded in the request trace.

Expected: On connection handoff or graceful close, the serving runtime should emit a terminal marker and all associated metadata prior to any socket teardown or proxy handoff so clients receive a complete final chunk.

Temporary impact mitigation requested by customer: recommend sticky sessions or disabling the specific edge health-rebind for the customer route while we investigate.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a long-running chat completion against redwood-1-large in eu-west with streaming over websocket and a large final choice (~2k tokens)
2) Configure a synthetic flappy-edge scenario: trigger a health-probe on the upstream edge to force a connection migration during response streaming
3) Observe the client WebSocket receiving the last token batch without an end_event and then a socket close from client side
4) Compare server traces and edge proxy logs for timestamp alignment of EOF and proxy handoff markers
logs: client: ws.recv -> '{ "choices": [{ "text": "...final sentence partial"' (no closing braces)
serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T09:41:22.835Z - write-stream EOF detected - upstream-socket-id=7f9c - request_id=req-8b2f
trace: trace_id=tr-20260310-7a - events: [start, token-batch, token-batch, EOF] (missing end_event)
nginx-edge: proxy: client_conn_rebind triggered by healthprobe, downstream_keepalive closed before graceful drain
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reports repeated truncated final chunks across ~0.8% of streams during peak. Provided initial logs and a sample ws capture.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Eng (Diego Morales): Noted correlation between proxy handoffs and EOFs; requested edge logs and nginx config for the affected flavor.

2026-03-10 14:08 - SRE (Lina Patel): Found an nginx setting (proxy_next_upstream_... on error) and a custom handshake timeout that can trigger rebind during long responses. Temporarily disabled rebind for AtlasApps route as a mitigation.

2026-03-11 09:33 - Eng (Diego Morales): Reproduced locally using forced connection migration; filing runtime change to ensure terminal marker emission before socket closure during handoff (PR linked).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The proxy performs an upstream rebind and closes the downstream socket before the serving runtime flushes the terminal metadata. The runtime assumes the transport flush completed and does not retry terminal-event emission.
Evidence: Trace shows EOF at the edge timestamped between two token batches and no subsequent end_event in the trace. Edge logs show connection handoff initiated by health probe within 3ms of EOF.
Risk: If terminal events are lost clients will re-request completions; this can double token usage and cause billing/latency blowups for affected customers.
Relevant configs: nginx edge flavor v1.14 had aggressive proxy_termination_on_rebind enabled; newer flavors have sticky-session preservation.
resolution: Mitigation applied: SRE disabled in-flight rebinds for AtlasApps route and applied sticky-session pinning to avoid mid-stream handoffs.
Fix planned: Engineering to land runtime change to treat terminal marker emission as idempotent and to retry emission on transient transport errors (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2491).
Follow-ups: Create a platform task to scan edge flavors for non-graceful handoff settings and add a monitoring alert for 'stream EOF without end_event' (INT-3347).
Customer communication: Notified AtlasApps of temporary mitigation and ETA for code fix; recommended they keep sticky sessions until fix is deployed.
